### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0c83f8f17a96656ce55ef1e605d51b2a20fe6c8b` — the merge of head `c965590cfc76df116ed986cb4401a52668d88125` into base `fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0c83f8f17a96656ce55ef1e605d51b2a20fe6c8b && git checkout 0c83f8f17a96656ce55ef1e605d51b2a20fe6c8b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773 c965590cfc76df116ed986cb4401a52668d88125 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773 && git merge --no-ff c965590cfc76df116ed986cb4401a52668d88125

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa9d695522925152815106605e5a612e331d2773` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read) · Head-sha: c965590cfc76df116ed986cb4401a52668d88125 · 2026-11-16T16:08Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, reading the final head declared in 6921783819. I read card #34396, dev report 6921083519, the PR body with its Acceptance notes, and the PR's own diff against the main it merged (`cfcba539`): 3 files, +475/−29. No L2 is owed: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and no file under `packages/objectql` changes.

- **Card relation.** `Fixes #34396`. The card's "expected" is that uninstalling a composed artifact's entry uninstalls every package body the install registered, with extending modules before the package they extend. That is what the PR builds, and it is the first of the card's two equivalent readings.
- **The unit.** `installedUnitPackageIds` reads the entry's stored body (`flattenPackageBody`). For a body with `packages[]`, it takes each member's id in the reverse of the rehydrate's own order (`orderHydrationBatch`, dependents first), deduplicated, and appends the entry's own id if no member carries it. A body without `packages` is the entry's id alone, so a single-package entry asks and withdraws exactly what it did before.
- **Refusal versus order.** `planUnitWithdrawal` asks the registry's one predicate (`assertPackageUninstallable`) of every member while the whole unit is still registered.
  - A `PackageUninstallExtendedError` whose causes (`extenders`, which the class always sets as an array, plus `customizationPackageId`) all lie inside the unit becomes an ordering constraint.
  - A cause outside the unit refuses the whole uninstall with the registry's own 409 sentence, before anything moves. So does a cycle of members that extend each other.
  - A throw that is not the coded 409 is left to the withdrawal, as before.
  - The pure planner places a member only after everything it waits on.
- **Withdrawal.** Each member's names are captured, then each is withdrawn, all synchronously (no `await` between the ledger removal and the last withdrawal). Object copies and extended-copy restores run per withdrawn member, and so do the uninstall cleanups, so a module's permission sets go with it. Handler unbind, `metadata:reloaded` and the `package_uninstall` row run once per entry, matching the one entry the install wrote.
- **Pins.** The new file `marketplace-install-local-composed-uninstall.test.ts` (8 tests) covers:
  - the reporter's 404 and read-only predicate on the module, with nothing moved;
  - the entry's DELETE answering 200 and withdrawing every member, module before app;
  - the module going first even when the artifact lists it ahead of the app;
  - a reinstall after uninstall, which is the recovery the card asked for;
  - an extension from a different install still answering 409 naming that package, with nothing moved, plus its CONTROL once that install is gone;
  - single-package withdrawal and its 409, as before.

  Per 6921083519 the file was red on `cfcba539` (4 failed, each the reporter's 409) and is 8/8 at head.
- **Changeset.** `patch` on `@objectstack/cloud-connection`. The three "what does not change" bullets match the code: a foreign extension or pair still gets 409, a single package is withdrawn alone, and a module still has no entry of its own.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 51 names, 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- **Base.** PRBASE is `fa9d6955` (Test Core plan), so K = 1. Since then main gained #34403, which touches `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` too. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` is clean, and the two changes sit in different methods (the seed readers versus `handleUninstall`).

### Notes (not blocking)

- **Partial withdrawal.** If one member's withdrawal is refused after others have been withdrawn, the handlers bound for the whole install stay bound (`unbindArtifactHandlers` runs only when none was refused), and the withdrawn members' handlers stay with them until restart. The refused member is reported on `cleanups`, and the log names the members that were withdrawn. This is acceptable as reported. A sentence in Acceptance notes would make it visible.
- **Already recorded in Acceptance notes and not built:** a member extended by both a same-unit module and a foreign package gets a sentence that also names the same-unit module; and per-member uninstall guards. Both are accepted as recorded.

Landing: not Tier H. Area o1-B lands it. If #34403 lands first, re-check that the merge is still clean on the landing head.
